simple.meaning: מַחְתֶּרֶת (machtereth) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a burglary ; figuratively, unexpected examination.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Exodus, Jeremiah, beginning at Exodus 22:1. Its contexts include blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַחְתֶּרֶת (H4290).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַחְתֶּרֶת (machtereth) / H4290 is traced through Exodus 22:1, Jeremiah 2:34 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4290. machtereth מַחְתֶּ֫רֶת noun masculine breaking in, burglary — ׳אִםבַּֿמּ הַגַּנָּב יִמָּצֵא Exod 22:1 i.e. caught in the act (JE); so בַּמּ ׳לֹא מְצָאתִים Jer 2:34 , not in the act of breaking in didst thou find them (2 feminine singular suffix Ges § 44 , 2, R 4), i.e. those whom thou hast slain were not detected in crime.
